newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli soldier fires in Hebron, wounds eight.
newsitem.headline: Israeli soldier fires in Hebron, wounds eight.

text.p: An Israeli soldier sprayed bullets at Arabs in a Hebron market on Wednesday, wounding eight in an attempt to sabotage the imminent handover of the West Bank town to Palestinian rule.
The off-duty soldier, wearing the skullcap of a religious Jew, emptied the clip of his M-16 automatic rifle into the crowded produce market before other soliders overpowered him, witnesses said.
"Even after soldiers had wrestled him to the ground he tried to put a second magazine into his gun," said Reuters cameraman Mazen Dana.
Israeli security sources identified the gunman as Noam Friedman from the Maale Adumim settlement near Jerusalem.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu condemned the shooting in a call to Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and vowed to implement their peace deals, an aide to Arafat said. But negotiations due to resume at noon (1000 GMT) on Wednesday were postponed.
"I want to say again in a sharp way that no crime and no violent act will stand in the way of our completing the work," Netanyahu told reporters.
The gunman told investigators he wanted to sabotage the handover, Israel's central area commander Major-General Uzi Dayan told army radio.
The army placed armoured personnel carriers on the hills above Hebron after the shooting and Palestinian youths threw stones and burned tyres near a hospital where some of the wounded were taken.

"There are eight wounded. One was in critical condition and was sent to Hadassah hospital (in Jerusalem). We thought he died but he didn't. He is in bad condition," Jibril Rajoub, chief of Palestinian security in the West Bank, told Reuters.
The centre of the city, where some 400 Jewish settlers live in heavily guarded enclaves among 100,000 Arabs, was closed.
Hebron has been a powderkeg since settler Baruch Goldstein massacred 29 Moslems in 1994 into the al-Ibrahimi mosque at the Cave of the Patriarchs, a site holy to Jews and Moslems.

"It happened right in front of me," said vegetable seller Walid Kafisheh, 46. "I tried to stop him but the soldiers got to him first. Then soldiers and police came from everywhere shooting," he told Reuters.
Witnesses said soldiers guarding the Avraham Avinu settlement nearby fired into the market thinking they were under attack. At least one Palestinian was hit by that fire, witnesses said.
Israeli lieutenant Avi Buskila grabbed the soldier.

"He entered the area at the square and began shooting into the vegetable market. I stood at my post and heard the shots. Within 10 seconds I pinned him to the ground and took his gun," he told Reuters.
Netanyahu said earlier on Wednesday he and Arafat had yet to fix a summit to sew up a deal giving self-rule to Hebron.
Security concerns and other issues have delayed the handover of most of Hebron to the Palestinians.

Jewish settlers in the town had said they were praying for a miracle to prevent Israeli troops from pulling back and warned of impending bloodshed. They scuffled with Palestinians on Tuesday and tried to take over Arab houses in the casbah.
"I appeal even at this moment to the prime minister: Don't sign an agreement that will endanger our lives," Hebron leader Rabbi Moshe Levinger told Israel Radio before the shooting.

But chief Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat told army radio: "We have always been arguing with the Israeli government, and the previous government actually, that the real threat to peace is not the Palestinians.
"It's these settlers, these Israeli settlers," he said.
Jewish settlers, who number 130,000 in the West Bank and Gaza Strip, helped Netanyahu sweep to power in elections last May on a promise to be tough with the Palestinians.

But Netanyahu has come under pressure from Washington, Israel's closest ally, to honour peace deals and withdraw from Hebron, the last of seven West Bank towns due for self-rule under the first stage of the 1993 Oslo peace accord.
Hebron settlers' spokesman Noam Arnon told Reuters the shooting pointed to the need for Israel to retain total control.
He said that if Palestinian police had been deployed, there could have been clashes between the PLO and Israelis after such an incident.
